newsitem.title: USA: Intel to cut prices on MMX chips-- report.
newsitem.headline: Intel to cut prices on MMX chips-- report.

text.p: Intel Corp will aggressively cut prices on large orders for its MMX semiconductor chips, according to a report by online news service ZD Net.

The report caused some skittishness about Intel's upcoming earnings, traders said. Goldman Sachs downgraded 1997 profit estimates for Intel slightly, to $8.50 from $8.70. It left 1998 estimates unchanged, according to market sources.
ZD Net said Intel will cut prices for orders of 1,000 units or more by roughly 35 to 50 percent, citing sources near the firm.
"That's a bit steeper than I expected," said Scott Randall, semiconductor analyst at Soundview Financial.

But he cautioned against making too much hay out of the price cuts. "Volume discounts are nothing new, though. They are more aggressive, but the real thing to pay attention to is if PCs move down as a result."
He also said that Intel was not likely to make a formal announcement, because the prices might have been intended for a few customers and not part of an overall strategy.
Intel was not immediately available for comment.
Intel will cut prices on the 233MHz chip to $378 from $594; the 200MHz chip to $247 from $492; and the 166 MHz will be cut to $142 from $270, according to ZD Net.
It said 166 MHz chips will go to $341 from $508; 150 MHz chips to $236 from $336; and a new 133 MHz will be priced at $176. The price cuts take effect on July 28, the report said.
Shares of Intel opened sharply lower on the Nasdaq, at 143, down 4-1/2 from a closing price of 147-1/2.
